findings.why: The Day 1 / 12 hours later / Week 2 frames are an AI-generated time-lapse set beside the 12-hour stat; AI frames are not representative, unretouched evidence and the "not real results" note sits only in the footnote.
findings.fix: Replace the timeline with a product or texture visual and keep the 12-hour statement only as the footnoted perception finding, or use real, unretouched study images with their qualifier.

findings.why: The headline promises something at "12 hours and two weeks", but the only stat on the ad is the 12-hour one; the page's only 2-week stat (F18) is about reduced irritation and is not shown, so "two weeks" implies a result with no study or qualifier on the creative.
findings.fix: Drop "two weeks": "12 hours with 10% Vitamin B5", keeping the 12-hour perception statement in the footnote (or lead with "10% Vitamin B5 (Panthenol) for oil-free moisturization", as the page words it).

rule_hit_review.why: Matches F16 and keeps "agreed"; it needs study type and n on the creative, and the 12-hour duration is itself a time-bound claim the rule's pattern did not catch.

tone_read: Calm and spec-led with no fear or hype, and the footnote is candid that the frames are illustrations. The timeline format and the vague "two weeks" lean toward category transformation creative.
language_read: "10% Vitamin B5" is in house format and the 12-hour stat keeps the page's "subjects agreed" wording. "Two weeks" has no matching stat on the ad, so it reads as an unhedged outcome.
